verses.1: Hear this, the priests! Listen carefully. The house of Israel and the house of the king shall listen too. For you have been given judgment, just as you were expected to be. It is a punishment for your sins.
verses.2: And they slaughtered the sheep. I give them all to them.
verses.3: I knew that Ephraim and Israel would never be able to get away from me. Now, Ephraim has been buried, and Israel is in ruins.
verses.4: They shall not be allowed to return to their God, for the spirit of lust is in their hearts. They do not know Jehovah at all.
verses.5: And Gone-Yisrael answered him. And Israel and Ephraim will be destroyed in their rebellion, just as Judah was also destroyed along with them.
verses.6: In the evening and at dawn, they will go to seek Jehovah. But they will not find any escape from them.
verses.7: In Jehovah’s name, they said that strange children have been born now. They will eat their share of food soon.
verses.8: They set up a trumpet in the field; there was a loud noise. The house of Aon praised you, my Lord.
verses.9: Ephraim will be destroyed on the day of its downfall. I truly know this to be true.
verses.10: The priests of Judah were like people who were walking along the borders; flames of fire rushed over them, just like water flowing across their bodies.
verses.11: Ephraim acted in accordance with the law, because he obeyed the commands of God.
verses.12: And I have made Ephraim like a vineyard, and Judah like a fig tree.
verses.13: Ephraim saw its destruction, and Judah also saw its downfall. Ephraim went to Assyria, and he sent messengers to King Yerobeam. But he couldn’t heal you, nor could he bring you back from your ruin.
verses.14: For I am like a raven that flies over Ephraim; I am like a bird that roams through the house of Judah. I will go and seek refuge elsewhere, for there is no one to protect me.
verses.15: I will return to my place, until they correct their mistakes and ask for my forgiveness. Then they will be able to forgive me.
